introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2023. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.
- Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.
- Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.
- In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.
- If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.
- NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.corrige_markdown:
On the outline map, mark and name each item with a clear symbol.

![fig-2](gce-ol-geography-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_2.png)

| Item | Where to place it |
|---|---|
| (i) Southern low plateau | the South Cameroon plateau, a rolling plateau of about 600 to 700 m in the south, covering the Centre, South and East regions (Yaounde is on it) |
| (ii) Douala-Yaounde-Bertoua Highway | from Douala on the coast, through Edea, east to Yaounde, then east and north-east to Bertoua in the East region (draw it as a thick line and name it) |
| (iii) One major airport | Douala International Airport, or Yaounde-Nsimalen International Airport (others: Garoua, Maroua-Salak) |
| (iv) One industrial zone | the Douala industrial zone (Bassa and Bonaberi); other answers: Edea (aluminium smelter), Limbe |
| (v) Lake Chad | the extreme northern tip of the country, on the border with Chad and Nigeria |
| (vi) Waza National Park | in the Far North region, in the narrow north near the border with Chad |

Marks are given for correct location and for naming.

**(i) Urban centres.**

1. **Housing shortage and slums**, because of rapid rural-urban migration, with poor sanitation and waste disposal.
2. **Unemployment and traffic congestion**, with poor water and electricity supply and flooding in the rainy season.

**(ii) Exploitation of forest resources.**

1. **Illegal and uncontrolled logging**, which leads to deforestation and loss of wildlife habitat.
2. **Poor transport and high costs**, because logs must be taken out on poor forest roads that wash away, and only a few valuable species are taken, which wastes the rest.

**(iii) The tourist industry.**

1. **Poor infrastructure:** bad roads to the sites, a lack of good hotels and few airports.
2. **Insecurity, poor publicity and a lack of trained staff**, and poaching, which reduces the wildlife that attracts tourists.

**(iv) Road transport.**

1. **Poor state of the roads:** many are untarred and become impassable in the rainy season; potholes are common.
2. **Road accidents and high costs:** overloaded and old vehicles, bad driving and the high cost of maintaining roads and vehicles.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Outline THREE economic importance of the Atlantic Ocean to Cameroon.

[3 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Sea transport and trade:** the ports of Douala, Kribi (the deep-sea port) and Limbe handle most of the country's imports and exports (cocoa, timber, bananas, oil), and also serve landlocked Chad and the Central African Republic.
2. **Fishing:** the ocean gives fish and shrimps for food, jobs and export.
3. **Offshore oil and tourism:** offshore oil and gas fields yield government revenue, and beaches such as Kribi and Limbe attract tourists.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Briefly explain THREE difficulties in developing Air transport in Cameroon.

[3 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **High cost:** building and maintaining airports, runways and navigation equipment and buying aircraft needs a great deal of money, which the country does not easily have.
2. **Low demand and high fares:** most people have low incomes and cannot afford air tickets, so there are few passengers and few profitable routes, especially inside the country.
3. **Shortage of skilled staff and difficult conditions:** pilots, engineers and controllers need long expensive training, and poor weather (storms, harmattan haze) and poor equipment at small airports limit flights.
